reviewBoundary: Three whole-passage adult originals: ten-gap/fifteen-word CET4 and CET6 banks plus eight-gap C1 word formation. Fictional cases. Same-author lexical and variant review, not independent calibration. Unlisted written forms reviewable.

units.title: Walking home together
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose one word for each gap. Use each word at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: Walking home together
materials.text:
A group of students started walking home together after their evening classes. The original ____1____ was simple: anyone taking the same route could meet outside the library at nine. There was no requirement to attend every evening, and nobody had to explain why they wanted company.

The route had to be ____2____ for everyone joining it. A short flight of steps made one path inconvenient for a member with an injured knee, so the group chose a slightly longer route with a ____3____ surface. Saving a few minutes was not useful if one person could not comfortably follow.

Clear ____4____ helped newcomers find the meeting point. The group described a particular library entrance rather than assuming everyone knew which door was meant. They also made the departure time ____5____: the walk began at nine, not whenever the most impatient member wanted to leave.

Students were asked to send a message if they had said they were coming but were ____6____. Otherwise, the group might wait for someone who had made other plans. The message did not need a personal explanation; it only needed to prevent unnecessary ____7____.

The arrangement remained ____8____. People could join on one night and travel another way on the next. It was not a service promising an escort to every possible address. Members were encouraged to ____9____ the plan if a class timetable changed or the chosen path became unavailable.

Over time, the walks became a pleasant end to the day. Some evenings were full of conversation; others were quiet. What made the arrangement ____10____ was not a complicated system but a few shared expectations about where to meet, when to leave and how to communicate a change.

questions.explanation: Arrangement names the agreed meeting plan described next. Instructions are directions within a plan, damage harm, delay waiting and purchase buying; the other words do not name the overall setup.

Accessible fits a route usable by everyone including a person with a knee injury. Level refers to the surface chosen next, not overall access; optional concerns participation and fixed time. Other adjectives do not mean usable for all.

Level describes a surface without the inconvenient steps. Fixed concerns stability, fragile vulnerability and temporary duration; flexibly is an adverb. The other candidates do not name a step-free surface.

Instructions give newcomers the entrance and meeting-point directions. Arrangement is the overall plan, while delay/damage/purchase do not name directions. Other bank entries cannot be plural guidance here.

Fixed establishes nine as the settled departure time, contrasted with individual wishes. Temporary concerns duration, fragile vulnerability, and flexibly is an adverb rather than the required complement. Other bank adjectives do not set the agreed time.
Absent describes someone expected but not attending. Accessible refers to reachability, optional a choice and successful an outcome; the other entries do not express nonattendance.
Delay is unnecessary waiting for someone not coming. Damage is harm, purchase buying and arrangement the plan, not time lost waiting.

Optional means attendance is a choice night by night. Fixed imposes a settled arrangement, temporary concerns duration and accessible usability. Fragile concerns vulnerability, not voluntary attendance.
Reconsider means think about the plan again when conditions change. Purchase means buy, not review a plan; the remaining bank words do not supply the base verb needed after to.
Successful evaluates the arrangement’s useful outcome. Accessible concerns usability, optional choice, temporary duration and explicit disclosure; none names overall achievement as directly.

units.title: Allocating the small hall
units.instruction: Read the complete passage. Choose one word for each gap. Use each word at most once; five are not needed.

materials.title: Allocating the small hall
materials.text:
A local festival introduced a free discussion in a hall with limited seating. Previous events had used first-come booking, but organisers worried that this favoured people able to remain online at the exact release time. They proposed a lottery as an ____1____ method of allocating places.

The change did not increase the hall's ____2____. It changed how demand beyond that limit was handled. Organisers therefore needed to be ____3____ about what the lottery could and could not achieve. A more convenient application period was not the same as a guarantee that every applicant would attend.

Applications remained open for a week. Entries submitted on the first and last day had an ____4____ chance in the draw. This removed the advantage of speed within the application period, although it did not remove every possible ____5____. Someone who never heard about the event could still not apply.

The team published the selection ____6____, including how duplicate entries and cancellations would be handled. Accessibility requirements were considered separately rather than treated as an attempt to gain an unfair advantage. The aim was to distinguish practical support from a general ____7____ for a particular applicant.

After the draw, a waiting list provided a way to ____8____ seats released by cancellations. Organisers asked successful applicants to confirm attendance, while making clear that confirmation was not evidence of a paid purchase: the event remained free.

The final report described both the benefits and ____9____ of the new method. A lottery distributed a scarce opportunity differently; it did not make scarcity disappear. Keeping that distinction ____10____ helped people evaluate the policy without expecting it to solve every problem associated with access.

questions.explanation: Alternative means another method replacing first-come booking. Sequential means in order, simultaneous at the same time, compulsory required and central important; none expresses the replacement method.

Capacity names the hall’s maximum accommodation. Scarcity is insufficiency of places rather than the physical limit itself; exclusion nonparticipation, procedure method and preference favour do not name the hall’s seating limit.

Transparent about what a policy can achieve means open and clear about its limits. Alternative, equal, central, sequential, simultaneous and compulsory do not complete be ... about with that disclosure meaning; the other items have unsuitable grammatical roles.

An equal chance gives neither first nor last day an advantage. Alternative concerns a different method, compulsory a requirement, simultaneous timing and sequential order; none expresses equal probability.

Exclusion names being unable to participate because the person never heard. Scarcity is limited supply, preference favour and limitations the later general drawbacks. Other entries do not name missing the application opportunity.
Procedure covers the published rules for duplicates and cancellations. Preference is favour, capacity seats and scarcity limited supply; other nouns do not name the selection steps.

Preference for a particular applicant means favouring that person. Accessibility support is distinguished from such favour. Exclusion is keeping someone out, procedure rules and capacity supply, not personal advantage.
Reallocate means assign released seats to waiting applicants. Withdraw would remove seats rather than give them to replacements; other entries are not base verbs for redistribution.

Limitations are the method’s bounds, paired with benefits. Exclusion is one possible access problem but singular/uncountable and not the plural summary of several bounds; capacity is hall size, scarcity shortage and preference favour.

Keeping the distinction central means treating it as a main consideration in evaluating the policy. Transparent is already required at gap3 and cannot be reused; the remaining adjectives do not express the distinction’s importance to evaluation.

units.title: Starting to speak together
units.instruction: Use the word in brackets to form one word that fits each gap.

materials.title: Starting to speak together
materials.text:
Several complete ____1____ (BEGIN) joined our adult conversation group. A degree of ____2____ (CERTAIN) was natural: nobody knew what the first meeting would require. The organiser avoided asking everyone to make a long speech immediately.

Instead, we worked in pairs to plan an imaginary day out. The task required ____3____ (COOPERATE), since each person held different information about opening times and travel. A confident speaker could not simply supply every answer without listening.

As I became more ____4____ (DEPEND), I stopped waiting for the organiser to choose every word for me. When I did need help, I asked her ____5____ (DIRECT) rather than sending a question through my partner. That small change made the exchange feel more like an ordinary conversation.

Speaking fluently at once had seemed ____6____ (POSSIBLE): I could barely introduce myself. Breaking the activity into manageable decisions allowed us to participate before we felt fully ready. Our confidence improved ____7____ (GRADUAL), through repeated attempts rather than a sudden transformation.

At the end, each pair described its plan. The result was a shared ____8____ (ACHIEVE), not proof that we had mastered the language. We had simply found a way to use what we knew and discover what we still needed.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with one word formed from BEGIN.
questions.explanation: Several complete beginners uses a plural count noun for novice people. Beginner is singular and beginning an event/time.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one word formed from CERTAIN.
questions.explanation: A degree of uncertainty names the initial lack of confidence. Certain and certainly are adjective/adverb forms.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one word formed from COOPERATE.
questions.explanation: Required takes a noun for joint work: cooperation, also standard hyphenated co-operation. Adjective/adverb forms do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one word formed from DEPEND.
questions.explanation: More independent describes a person able to make decisions. Independence is a noun and independently an adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one word formed from DIRECT.
questions.explanation: Directly modifies asked. Direct is adjective and direction noun; indirect forms would reverse the stated choice not to send a message through someone else.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with one word formed from POSSIBLE.
questions.explanation: Barely being able to introduce oneself makes immediate fluency seem impossible. Possibility is a noun and possibly an adverb; neither serves as the adjective complement here.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one word formed from GRADUAL.
questions.explanation: Gradually modifies improved. Gradual is adjective and graduation a different noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one word formed from ACHIEVE.
questions.explanation: A shared achievement names an accomplished result. Achieve is verb and achievable adjective.
